facility_roles.quote: We report the detection of polarized anisotropy in the Cosmic Microwave Background radiation with the Degree Angular Scale Interferometer (DASI), located at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole research station.

intervals.label: deployment
intervals.note: Season wording only ("1999--2000 austral summer"); the interval is stored at January 2000 with the season in `display`.
intervals.quote: The telescope was deployed at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole research station during the 1999--2000 austral summer and conducted observations of the CMB throughout the following austral winter.

end.note: last season reported in the 2004 three-year paper

intervals.label: observations
intervals.note: First observations were made through the 2000 austral winter; polarization observations followed in 2001-2003 (abstract of astro-ph/0409357: data "throughout the 2003 season"). No source consulted states when DASI stopped observing; 2003 is the last season it reports.
intervals.quote: The telescope was deployed at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole research station during the 1999--2000 austral summer and conducted observations of the CMB throughout the following austral winter.

intervals.label: observations ended
intervals.note: Inferred terminal event: the 2004 paper analyses "the complete 3-year data set"; no fetched source states an end-of-observations or decommissioning date.
intervals.quote: We present the analysis of the complete 3-year data set obtained with the Degree Angular Scale Interferometer (DASI) polarization experiment

quantity.quote: DASI is a 13-element, co-planar interferometric array operating in ten 1-GHz bands spanning 26 − 36 GHz.

name: DASI
notes: No collaboration record: none of the DASI papers read (astro-ph/0104488, 0104489, 0209478, 0409357) names a "DASI Collaboration"; they are signed by individual authors at the University of Chicago, UC Berkeley and collaborators.
No official website is recorded: astro.uchicago.edu/dasi now redirects to the University of Chicago department home page, which says nothing about DASI.
No INSPIRE experiment id is recorded: INSPIRE was not contacted by this stream.

physics_goals.quote: a compact microwave interferometer designed to measure anisotropy in the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) on degree and sub-degree scales (l=100--900)
physics_goals.value: Measure CMB anisotropy on degree and sub-degree scales (multipoles l = 100-900) and, from 2001, its polarization.

summary.plain: A compact microwave interferometer at the South Pole that measured the Big Bang afterglow on degree scales in 2000 and, in 2002, made the first detection of its polarization.
summary.technical: Degree Angular Scale Interferometer (13 elements, 26-36 GHz, l = 100-900) at the South Pole (MAPO); deployed 1999-2000 austral summer; first-season power spectrum (2001), first CMB polarization detection (2002), three-year polarization results to the 2003 season (2004).
